sourceEvidence.label: ObraSaaS PRO-05 product, source and privacy evidence

assessment.summary: The reviewed source supports one cross-cutting opportunity: centralize tenant-scoped privacy discovery, retention decisions and verified execution before accepting real labour data.

nonNegotiables: No generic or automatic destructive deletion is introduced before each data domain is classified and tested.
Existing append-only labour, payment and security evidence remains fail-closed.
Every request and discovered resource remains bound to one organization and one canonical subject.
Primary-database completion never implies provider or backup completion.
assumptions: PostgreSQL and the existing Vercel cron remain the operational platform for the first phase.
No measured throughput, latency or memory budget was supplied.
Jurisdiction-specific retention periods require legal approval before destructive execution.

opportunities.title: Centralize privacy lifecycle control
opportunities.summary: Create one tenant-scoped control plane that discovers subject data, records retention decisions, blocks on unknown scope and verifies domain and provider outcomes.
opportunities.diagnosis: Privacy obligations currently span relational records, untyped JSON, storage, WhatsApp, AI providers and backups, while only isolated lifecycle jobs own bounded subsets. Public language therefore outruns machine-verifiable behavior.

evidence.claim: The worker and platform-user graphs mix Cascade, Restrict and NoAction relations and include encrypted identity, financial, geolocation, message, media and derived AI data.
The public page states 30-day operational deletion and normally 90-day backup purge, but no repository-wide workflow enforces or proves those statements.
One transient onboarding domain already uses bounded SKIP LOCKED selection, atomic cryptographic erasure and PII-free audit records.
The product traceability matrix marks PRO-05 absent and a gate before real labour data.
Because subject identity can occur in typed relations, raw channel identifiers and JSON/provider payloads, a generic ORM cascade cannot provide complete or safe erasure.

desiredInvariants: Every privacy case is bound to exactly one organization and canonical subject type; an authenticated tenant administrator may start non-destructive inventory, while verified requester identity or representation is mandatory before decision or action.
Discovery is read-only, repeatable and emits a hash-bound manifest containing no raw sensitive values, ciphertext, bearer tokens or provider credentials.
Unknown JSON, storage, provider or backup scope makes the case incomplete rather than silently successful.
Every resource ends in an explicit action class: export, erase, cryptographic erase, pseudonymize, restrict, keep with basis, legal hold or external-provider deletion.
No mutation runs until an authorized human approves a versioned manifest and all applicable holds and retention bases have been evaluated.
A case reaches verified completion only when every required domain and external processor has a terminal, evidence-backed outcome.

options.title: Truthful manual intake and domain runbooks
options.summary: Correct unsupported public promises and operate existing bounded purge routines through a reviewed manual checklist.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The public wording can immediately be made truthful.
A runbook reduces accidental deletion but cannot prove complete graph coverage.
Manual handling does not close the machine-verifiable PRO-05 gate.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removing unsupported promises and requiring review reduces unsafe ad hoc deletion, but coverage still depends on operator memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise the runbook against synthetic worker and platform-user cases and record missed domains.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new runtime query path is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm that only static content and documentation changed.

tradeoffs.assessment: No additional in-process state is retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No memory benchmark is required beyond normal build validation.

tradeoffs.assessment: A checklist can reduce operator error, but manual handoffs remain non-atomic and difficult to replay.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a tabletop case twice and compare outcomes and evidence.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each case consumes expert time and has no automated deadline, backlog or provider reconciliation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure handling time and unresolved steps during synthetic cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: It is immediately reversible and prepares the classification vocabulary for later automation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review the runbook vocabulary against the future manifest schema.

workPackages: Create a reviewed manual classification and evidence checklist.
acceptanceCriteria: The public page makes no unimplemented technical deadline claim.
A synthetic case has an explicit unresolved status for every unknown domain.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the static wording and runbook changes.

options.title: Incremental tenant privacy control plane
options.summary: Add PostgreSQL-backed cases, immutable discovery manifests, legal holds and domain-owned idempotent adapters while retaining one deployable application.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Truthful public intake can point to a durable, traceable case without overstating completion.
A catalog and domain adapters make mixed relational and non-relational coverage explicit.
The existing bounded transaction pattern can be retained as one adapter rather than replaced.
It supplies the control plane, but PRO-05 remains open until destructive adapters, providers and restore drills are proven.
WhatsApp raw identifiers and provider deletion still require dedicated adapters and migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: One tenant-scoped state machine owns discovery completeness, approvals, holds and terminal evidence while domain adapters preserve local invariants.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove cross-tenant denial, manifest integrity, zero-mutation discovery and fail-closed unknown domains in tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Discovery adds bounded count and identifier queries, but it stays off interactive WhatsApp and dashboard hot paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark synthetic tenants at expected and upper-bound row counts; paginate every adapter.

tradeoffs.assessment: Manifest creation allocates bounded pages and canonical summaries; persistent items grow with discovered domains and resources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and manifest row growth with large synthetic subjects; enforce page and payload limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durable per-domain states make retries idempotent and partial provider failure visible instead of collapsing into a false global success.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject transaction, storage and provider failures and verify replay without duplicate actions.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing application and cron can expose backlog, deadlines and blockers without introducing a new service, although the domain catalog becomes an owned operational asset.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add backlog, overdue, blocked-domain and provider-pending metrics and run an operator tabletop.

tradeoffs.assessment: Schema, catalog and adapters must roll out additively; destructive execution remains disabled until each domain and legal policy is approved.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Apply migrations from zero and upgrade fixtures, then canary read-only discovery before enabling any action adapter.

residualRisks: Unclassified JSON until each catalog entry is reviewed
Provider deletion semantics and receipts vary
Backup restoration can resurrect data without tombstone replay
Legal retention decisions require local counsel

workPackages: Add cases and immutable read-only discovery manifests.
Add verified identity and decision workflow.
Implement domain-owned action adapters behind feature gates.
Add provider propagation and backup tombstone reconciliation.
acceptanceCriteria: Discovery is tenant-isolated, idempotent and mutation-free.
No action can run without a verified requester, approved manifest and evaluated holds.
Primary, provider and backup outcomes remain separately visible.
migrationNotes: Additive tables and enums first; no existing row rewrite.
Keep destructive execution disabled through the discovery-only phase.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable privacy execution and discovery feature gates; preserve additive case evidence for review, then revert application callers before removing schema.

options.title: Dedicated privacy orchestration service
options.summary: Move case state, provider credentials and deletion orchestration into a separately deployed least-privilege service.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A durable service can back truthful intake, but the current page still requires an immediate wording fix.
Isolation centralizes orchestration, while each domain still needs a safe local adapter.
The existing local job can be invoked through a constrained adapter.
Service isolation alone does not prove retention rules, providers or restore behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separate credentials and network policy can reduce blast radius, but cross-service authority and message authentication become new privileged boundaries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model service identity, adapter authorization, replay and credential scopes before implementation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Network hops and queueing add latency to discovery and execution, although these are asynchronous paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end case latency and queue depth under synthetic load.

tradeoffs.assessment: A separate runtime duplicates framework, connection-pool and queue-worker overhead.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure idle and peak memory of both deployments.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves, but distributed transactions, queues and credential rotation introduce more partial-failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run provider outage, duplicate delivery and database partition fault tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second deployment needs independent observability, on-call ownership, secrets, queues and release coordination.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Estimate operational ownership and complete a deployment/rollback drill.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing local domain logic needs authenticated adapters and dual-run reconciliation before authority can move safely.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Shadow read-only discovery and compare manifests before any cutover.

residualRisks: Higher operational complexity before product scale justifies it

workPackages: Define service identity and capability contract.
Build shadow discovery and manifest comparison.
Migrate action authority after parity and fault testing.
acceptanceCriteria: The service has no broad application-database credential.
Every command is tenant-, case-, manifest- and action-bound.
Duplicate or reordered messages cannot repeat a destructive action.
migrationNotes: Requires shadow mode and dual-read reconciliation.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Route new cases back to the in-application control plane while draining authenticated commands and preserving case evidence.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the incremental control plane now: it materially improves completeness and evidence without paying the distributed-systems cost of a separate orchestrator. Revisit service isolation when deletion volume, team ownership or credential-separation requirements justify it.

openQuestions: Which entity is controller and processor for each treatment and tenant contract?
Which labour, tax, accounting and litigation retention periods apply in each launch jurisdiction?
Which storage, messaging, AI, logging and backup subprocessors will be active in the pilot?
What verified privacy contact and operational owner should replace the personal inbox before production?
